x: M.N. Roy first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly in 1934. Nehru, Patel and Ambedkar became leading members of the Assembly later, but none of them proposed the idea first.
t: Recall who originated the idea, not who later led the Assembly.

x: Option C is incorrect: the elections were held in July–August 1946, not June–July. The other details are right: 389 planned seats (296 British India + 93 Princely States), 292 + 4 seats within British India, and one member per 10 lakh population.
t: Check each figure and date; the trap is a shifted month range.

x: Both are true and R explains A: the Assembly was elected indirectly because its members were chosen by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies, not by the people directly.
t: Ask whether the method of election in R is what makes A indirect.

x: Nehru chaired the Union Constitution Committee, Sardar Patel the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal Areas, J.B. Kripalani the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee and Dr. Rajendra Prasad the Steering Committee. The trap is swapping Patel (Advisory Committee) with Kripalani (its Sub-Committee).
t: Fix the one chair you are surest of, then eliminate codes.

x: All four are correct: 389 seats were planned (296 for British India, 93 for the Princely States), one member per 10 lakh population, and the Assembly had 15 women members.
t: Verify each number of the Assembly's composition separately.

x: The Objectives Resolution was moved on 13 December 1946 and adopted on 22 January 1947; the Drafting Committee was formed on 29 August 1947 and the Constitution adopted on 26 November 1949. So the order is D, A, B, C — moving always comes before adopting.
t: Anchor the dates; a resolution is moved before it is adopted.

x: Dr. Rajendra Prasad chaired three of them: the Steering Committee, the Rules of Procedure Committee and the ad-hoc Flag Committee. The Union Powers Committee was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru.
t: Assign each committee's chair and count; Nehru's committees are the trap.

x: Both are true: B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly and prepared its first draft, which had 243 Articles and 13 Schedules.
t: Check the role and the draft's numbers (243 Articles, 13 Schedules).

x: The Swaraj Party made the first formal demand at the Ranchi Conference (May 1934); Congress demanded it officially at Patna (May 1934); Nehru made a clear statement for it in 1938; the August Offer of 1940 accepted the principle. Ranchi and Patna in the same month are the trap.
t: Separate the two May 1934 demands by party and place.

x: Both are true: the Cripps Mission (1942) made the final proposal for an elected Constituent Assembly, and the Assembly was actually constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946.
t: Distinguish the mission that proposed from the plan that constituted.

x: All four are correct: Congress won 208 seats, the Muslim League 73 and others 15, and the Assembly was not elected on adult franchise.
t: Check each seat figure and the franchise basis.

x: Both are true and R explains A: the 1935 Act franchise was restricted precisely because voting depended on tax, education and property qualifications.
t: See whether R states the basis of the restriction in A.

x: Both are true: the Princely States at first stayed away and began joining the Assembly from its third session in April 1947.
t: Recall the session and month when the Princely States joined.

x: All four are correct: the first meeting was on 9 December 1946 with Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha as Temporary (Provisional) President, and Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected Permanent President on 11 December 1946.
t: Distinguish the temporary and permanent Presidents and their dates.

x: Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution at the fifth meeting of the first session (13 December 1946). It belongs to the first session, so options naming the second or eleventh session are wrong.
t: Locate the event in the first session of the Assembly.

x: All four are correct: the Constitution was adopted on the last day of the eleventh session, signed at the last meeting on 24 January 1950, came into force on 26 January 1950, and the work took 2 years, 11 months and 17 days.
t: Check each date and the duration of the Assembly's work.

x: All three are correct: the Assembly held 11 sessions over 165 sitting days, and its final meeting was on 24 January 1950.
t: Verify the session count, sitting days and final date.

x: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was both Permanent President and Chairman, so the same code (iii) appears twice; Frank Anthony was the first temporary Deputy Chairman and H.C. Mukherjee the first permanent Vice-President. Ambedkar headed the Drafting Committee, not the Assembly.
t: Allow a repeated code when one person held two posts.

x: Both are true: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee, which had six other members besides him.
t: Recall the chairman and the size of the Drafting Committee.

x: All six were the other members of the Drafting Committee: Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar, N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, K.M. Munshi, Mohammad Saadullah, B.L. Mitter and D.P. Khaitan. With Ambedkar as Chairman, it had seven members in all.
t: Count the members excluding the Chairman.

x: Both are true but unrelated: B.L. Mitter was replaced by N. Madhava Rao and D.P. Khaitan by T.T. Krishnamachari. One replacement does not explain the other.
t: Two true but independent facts: R cannot explain A.

x: Sardar Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee, H.C. Mukherjee the Minorities Sub-Committee, Nehru the States Committee and K.M. Munshi the Order of Business Committee. Option A wrongly gives the Minorities Sub-Committee to Nehru.
t: Fix Patel and Munshi first, then decide between Nehru and Mukherjee.
